conventions: Published points use the Binohash paper's accounting. It counts a signature that is n bytes short as 8n + 2 bits of work; this evaluator counts 8n, because the interpreter also accepts the negated nonce and values of s that wrap around the group order, which quadruples the accepted sighashes (spec/SECURITY-MODEL.md, section 3). The paper counts honest work in sighash evaluations and assumes every round has a solution; this evaluator counts SHA-256 compressions and the retries when a round has none. The paper's byte count is the locking script alone; the evaluator adds the unlocking script. Security and work figures are therefore not comparable cell for cell: `securityBitsPaperFormula` is the paper's section 5.3 formula evaluated with the evaluator's puzzle bits; `securityBitsEvaluator` adds the attacker who abandons a transaction after a round without a solution, and is what ledger rows carry.
